TEXT (text_source=study_materials): P.6 has one stem shared by all 13 outlets, so the stem goes in instructions and item_text is the outlet name as printed in the questionnaire grid (numbering '01.'..'13.' stripped). The questionnaire PDFs are image-only scans; the wording was read visually from 300-dpi renders of page 2 (crop_p6_stem_A/B.png, crop_p6_table_A/B.png) -- spot-check advisable. Versions A and B print P.6 identically (compared side by side; FT2973 says the versions differ only in P.9, 12, 15, 21, 24, 26, 29). DEVIATIONS: (1) p601 ships the questionnaire's 'TVE 1 (La 1)', which is what the interviewer read; the ES2973 variable label reads 'TVE (La 1)' -- same channel, the only label/questionnaire difference among the 13. (2) Dropped from instructions: 'P.6' numbering, the interviewer direction '(MOSTRAR TARJETA C).' (sibling precedent), and the interviewer-only instruction 'ENTREVISTADOR/A: LEER UNA A UNA LAS CADENAS ROTANDO EL ORDEN EN CADA ENTREVISTA' -- i.e. outlets were read one by one in rotated order, so presentation order varied across respondents; the rotation start ('Ítem por el que se comienza', P614, cols 68-69) is not in the table. Line wraps joined. No filter precedes P.6; all respondents were asked. OPTIONS: ES2973 VALUE LABELS identical on P601..P613 (asserted): 1 'Muy de izquierdas' 2 'Más bien de izquierdas' 3 'Ni de izquierdas ni de derechas' 4 'Más bien de derechas' 5 'Muy de derechas' 8 'N.S.' 9 'N.C.'; TARJETA C (Preg.6) text layer in both tarjetas PDFs reads the same five labels in capitals, and the questionnaire lists them 1..5; option_text ships the value labels' mixed case. All 13 items use all five levels. public_note: Codes run 1 = Muy de izquierdas (very left-wing) to 5 = Muy de derechas (very right-wing); don't-know and no-answer (very common here, 30-62% per outlet) are stored as missing; outlets were read in a rotated order per interview; English is IRW machine translation of the Spanish-only CIS questionnaire
